black-turtle-bean.name: Black beans

sections.whatItOffers: Black turtle beans are small, dense, earthy beans. Half a cup gives about 7.7 g of protein and 7.7 g of fibre, with folate (20% of the reference), potassium and plant iron.
sections.howToEatIt: Simmer into soups, stews and chilli, mash for burritos and tacos, or add to rice and salads. Canned beans, rinsed, are a shortcut.
sections.cycleRelevance: Iron needs are higher for women aged 19 to 50 (18 mg a day, against 8 mg for men), partly because of menstrual blood loss (NIH ODS). Black beans add plant iron, which is absorbed less readily than iron from meat; vitamin C in the same meal helps. No phase-specific claim is made.

kidney-bean.name: Kidney bean

sections.whatItOffers: Kidney beans are large, meaty beans with folate (about 29% of the reference in half a cup), potassium and magnesium, plus 7.7 g of protein and 5.7 g of fibre.
sections.howToEatIt: Use in chilli, curries, salads and stews. Dried kidney beans must be soaked and boiled hard before eating (see the caution); canned beans are already cooked.
sections.cycleRelevance: Folate is a nutrient some women of childbearing age do not get enough of (NIH ODS); Kidney beans are a good source. No phase-specific claim is made.

source.usdaDescription: Beans, kidney, all types, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt

cautions.text: Dried kidney beans contain a natural toxin that raw or undercooked beans can release. Soak them for at least 5 hours, pour the water away, then boil in fresh water for at least 30 minutes.
cautions.source: FDA, Natural Toxins in Food (content current as of 09/26/2024; read 2026-10-28); FDA, Bad Bug Book, 2nd edition: Phytohaemagglutinin (kidney bean lectin) (read 2026-10-29) (supports the existing caution)

cautions.text: Do not cook dried kidney beans in a slow cooker: it may not get hot enough to destroy the toxin.
cautions.source: FDA, Bad Bug Book, 2nd edition: Phytohaemagglutinin (kidney bean lectin) (read 2026-10-29) (supports the existing caution)

cautions.text: Canned kidney beans are already cooked and contain only low levels of the toxin.
cautions.source: FDA, Natural Toxins in Food (content current as of 09/26/2024; read 2026-10-28) (supports the existing caution)

kidney-bean.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).

red-lentil.name: Red lentil

sections.whatItOffers: Red lentils are quick-cooking, split lentils. The figures here are for the dry lentils: a quarter cup before cooking gives 11.5 g of protein and 5.2 g of fibre, with folate, zinc and iron (20% of the reference).
sections.practicalServing: ¼ cup dry, before cooking (USDA: 1 cup = 192 g)
sections.howToEatIt: Simmer for about 15–20 minutes into soups and dals, where they dissolve into a soft purée. They roughly triple in weight when cooked, so a cooked portion has about a third of these amounts.
sections.cycleRelevance: Iron needs are higher for women aged 19 to 50 (18 mg a day, against 8 mg for men), partly because of menstrual blood loss (NIH ODS). Red lentils add plant iron, which is absorbed less readily than iron from meat; vitamin C in the same meal helps. No phase-specific claim is made.

farro.name: Farro

sections.whatItOffers: Farro is a chewy ancient wheat grain. The figures here are for the dry, pearled grain: 45 g before cooking gives zinc (22% of the reference), magnesium, 5.7 g of protein and 3.3 g of fibre.
sections.practicalServing: 45 g dry, before cooking (USDA reference amount)
sections.howToEatIt: Simmer for 15–30 minutes until tender but chewy, then use in grain salads, soups and risottos. Whole farro takes longer than pearled and has more fibre.
sections.cycleRelevance: No cycle-phase claim is made for farro. It contains gluten, as it is a form of wheat.
